pdfAcquisition: Each original PDF downloaded from its official bchydro.com URL on 2026-10-30; every SHA-256 equals the hash recorded by the earlier Hydro recovery (captures/*.json expectedPdfSha256FromEarlierPackage).
rowComparison: scripts/check_chc_pdf.py run against each original PDF: PyMuPDF and Poppler both reconstruct every named row, with no missing rows, no extra rows and no unparsed monetary lines. Results: pdf-verification/<year>.json. The two readers share reconstruction code, so this is not two independent extractions; the visual review below covers that limit.
comparatorFix: Poppler copies a BEL control character from the 2013/14 cover page into its XML, which the comparator now strips before parsing; no schedule text contains control characters.
summaryColumns: Read from word coordinates on each summary page: REMUNERATION header spans x 416-492 and amounts end at x 492; EXPENSES header spans x 523-570 and amounts end at x 570. Rows: consolidated total of employees at $75,000 or less, then Total; the employer EI/CPP line sits below Total, in the remuneration column only, and is not part of Total. These confirm the capture controls exactly.
visualReview: All 19 schedule pages rendered at 90 dpi (pdftoppm) and inspected: typeset two-column tables, initials then surname, page sequences complete (1 of N to N of N) for every year, summary pages as above. Spot comparisons of rendered values with the candidates agreed, including the two separate JW Anderson rows of 2014/15 and explicit $0 expenses. The 2017/18 schedule has no named rows: its only employee figures are the at-or-below-threshold aggregate, which equals its total.
residuals: Named rows minus (Total less the consolidated aggregate) are within $3 for remuneration and expenses in every year, as in the accepted BC Hydro schedules; they are left as published.
decision: Accepted for 2012/13 to 2016/17 as research/salaries/columbia-hydro-constructors (scripts/accept-chc-salaries.py). 2017/18 publishes no named rows and is not imported; it is not a year without employees.
